title: Nước Chấm
subtitle: vietnamese dipping sauce
excerpt: Nước chấm is the essential Vietnamese dipping sauce made from fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, garlic, and chilli. It is served alongside almost every Vietnamese dish and takes less than 5 minutes to make. This recipe makes about 200ml.
sourceNotes: Nước chấm is the most fundamental condiment in Vietnamese cooking. Every Vietnamese cook has their own ratio and every region has a slightly different style . the south tends sweeter, the north more austere.

recipe.batchNotes: Make a double batch and keep in the fridge for up to 5 days. The flavour mellows and improves after a few hours.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to 5 days ahead. Keep refrigerated. The garlic will mellow.

glossaryTerms.definition: Vietnamese fish sauce, made by fermenting small fish with salt for months to years. It is the backbone of Vietnamese cooking and the key ingredient in nước chấm.
The defining principle of nước chấm. The ratio of sugar, lime, fish sauce, and water can be adjusted to taste, but all four elements must be in balance.

content.text: Nước chấm is built on
nước mắm
fish sauce balanced with lime, sugar, and water.
The
sweet-sour-salty balance
is personal . taste and adjust until it is right for you.
This recipe makes about 200ml.
Use a good quality fish sauce. The difference between a cheap and a quality fish sauce is significant in a recipe where the fish sauce is the star.
What you need
Method
Combine the fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, and warm water in a small bowl.
Stir until the sugar is completely dissolved. Warm water helps the sugar dissolve quickly.
Add the minced garlic and sliced chilli.
Taste the sauce. It should be bright, salty, sweet, and slightly sour all at once. Adjust any element that feels too dominant.
If too salty, add more lime juice and a splash of water. If too sour, add a pinch of sugar. If too sweet, add a little more fish sauce.
Leave for 10 minutes before serving so the garlic and chilli can infuse. Serve at room temperature.

attrs.symptom: The sauce tastes flat and one-dimensional.
attrs.cause: The four elements are not in balance.
attrs.fix: Work through each element: add a squeeze of lime for brightness, a pinch of sugar for sweetness, a splash of fish sauce for depth, or more water to round it out.

attrs.symptom: The sauce is too fishy and pungent.
attrs.cause: Too much fish sauce was used or a low-quality brand was chosen.
attrs.fix: Dilute with more lime juice and water. For a milder sauce, use a good quality Vietnamese fish sauce rather than a cheap one.

attrs.symptom: The garlic tastes too sharp after a few hours.
attrs.cause: The garlic enzymes become more pungent over time in the acid.
attrs.fix: This is normal. If you prefer a milder sauce, add the garlic just before serving rather than making it ahead.

content.text: Where this dish lives
Nước chấm is found on every Vietnamese table, in every region of the country.
It is served alongside spring rolls, grilled meats, noodle salads, and steamed dishes.
The southern style is sweeter and the northern style uses less sugar.
Every family has a version they consider the correct one.
Learning to make a good nước chấm is the first lesson in Vietnamese cooking.
